title: Hangenberg event (end-Devonian extinction)
summary: The Hangenberg event was a short extinction crisis at the end of the Devonian, first defined in the Rhenish Mountains of Germany, where its type sections give a date of 359.3 ± 0.1 Ma. It hit free-swimming animals such as fish and ammonoids hardest and is linked to ocean anoxia, a brief intense glaciation and large sea-level changes. Marine life then stayed at low diversity for more than 20 million years.

uncertainty.note: Range is 359.3 ± 0.1 Ma from the Rhenish Mountains type sections as quoted by Bundy and Ekhoff (Boise State). The same page gives 360.0 ± 0.1 Ma for tuffs in the Exshaw Formation, Alberta, so other regions give older dates. Denayer and Prestianni (2020) say the late Famennian extinctions lasted one to several hundred thousand years. Years are Ma counted back from the present.

as_recorded.value: 359.3 ± 0.1 Ma, from the type sections in the Rhenish Mountains of Germany

importance.justification: A major end-Devonian extinction crisis, followed by a recovery the Palaeontological Association page calls the longest of any crisis.
